slides.title: Override Keyword Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the primary benefit of using the 'override' specifier on derived class methods?
options: Ensures at compile-time that the method correctly overrides a base virtual function
Speeds up function execution at runtime
Automatically allocates method memory on Heap
Prevents derived classes from overriding it further
slides.correctAnswer: Ensures at compile-time that the method correctly overrides a base virtual function

slides.title: Final Specifier on Classes
slides.prompt: What happens when a class is declared as 'class Base final {...}'?
options: No other class can inherit from Base
All members of Base become immutable const variables
Base can only be instantiated once (Singleton)
Virtual functions are disabled inside Base
slides.correctAnswer: No other class can inherit from Base

slides.title: Covariant Return Types
slides.prompt: What are covariant return types in C++ virtual function overriding?
options: An override can return a pointer/reference to a class derived from the base method's return type
An override must return void regardless of base function return type
An override can return any primitive scalar data type
An override can change the function return type to templates
slides.correctAnswer: An override can return a pointer/reference to a class derived from the base method's return type
